# Upstash customer data merchant

Use an existing Upstash Redis database as the source for the original Starforge
merchant. The operator declares the permitted keys, inputs, projected columns
and response limits. The original seller publishes those named products through
its payment challenge, developer documentation and generated customer client.

The Upstash transport sends the existing read-only Lua script through the
[documented REST interface](https://upstash.com/docs/redis/features/restapi).
It requests binary RESP2, keeping the same byte, decimal, null and cursor handling
as the native Redis connection. The query engine, seller, buyer and retained
release workflow are shared with the [Redis product](README.md).

## Create the merchant

Install a release containing this transport with the original runtime installer.
Select the original native payment dependencies with `--native` when running
payment mode. This HTTP source uses Node's native HTTPS fetch and introduces no
extra package dependency. An existing native Redis runtime can use it directly.

```sh
starforge redis init --directory /srv/merchant/upstash --transport upstash-rest
```

The command creates the original source, merchant plan and input files in a new
private directory. Replace the example endpoint in `source.json`:

```json
{
  "transport": "upstash-rest",
  "endpoint": "https://your-database.upstash.io",
  "tokenEnv": "UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_TOKEN"
}
```

This object is the source's `connection`. Obtain the database's HTTPS endpoint
and token from the operator's existing Upstash account. Supply the token through
the named environment variable or the original host's private environment file.
Keep the environment available to both the current merchant and its retained
release children. The source stores the variable name; prepared customer
documentation contains the public query contract.

The endpoint must be a root HTTPS URL under `upstash.io`, without credentials,
query parameters, fragments or an alternate port. Redirects are rejected before
a token can be forwarded elsewhere. HTTP and TCP connection fields are distinct;
a partial pair is rejected during the original source validation.

For production, use the database's read-only token or an appropriately restricted
ACL user's REST token. Upstash documents both token types and
[ACL token generation](https://upstash.com/docs/redis/features/restapi#rest-token-for-acl-users).
Its current [security guide](https://upstash.com/docs/redis/features/security)
places custom ACLs on paid databases. Select the account's existing access model
with its operator; an ordinary source connection never creates or upgrades a
database.

## Map the customer's data

The supplied source demonstrates four named products: a string value, selected
hash fields, a sorted ranking and a stream projection. Replace those fixed keys
and field mappings with the agreed customer schema. Typed parameters select only
the alternatives declared in the source. Keep atomic amounts as strings.

Each query runs the existing `EVAL_RO` script once. Its read and encoded-output
limits remain active. The transport also limits the downloaded RESP2 frame before
decoding it. A cancelled or expired query aborts its owned HTTP request; queued
work and concurrent requests use the existing source limits. Quota and rate
responses reach the original operator/customer error path, with a provider
`Retry-After` value when supplied.

```sh
starforge redis describe --source /srv/merchant/upstash/source.json
starforge redis preflight --source /srv/merchant/upstash/source.json
starforge redis query --source /srv/merchant/upstash/source.json \
  --query catalog --input /srv/merchant/upstash/input.json \
  --output /srv/merchant/upstash/catalog-first.json
```

Preflight executes the real provider's read-only scripting capability check.
Inspection identifies `Upstash REST` and `HTTPS_RESP2`. The same inspection
continues to identify the native driver and RESP2 for a TCP source.

Read the retained output and confirm its source fields with the customer before
publishing the product. Set the merchant plan's actual origin, recipient, asset,
atomic amount and accepted payment alternatives. Prepare and inspect the
original complete customer package:

```sh
starforge redis prepare --source /srv/merchant/upstash/source.json \
  --plan /srv/merchant/upstash/merchant-plan.json \
  --directory /srv/merchant/upstash/prepared-first
starforge redis verify --directory /srv/merchant/upstash/prepared-first
starforge redis start --directory /srv/merchant/upstash/prepared-first \
  --port 8423 --operations-port 8424
```

The existing start command accepts the reviewed facilitator configuration.
Its developer portal includes the original OpenAPI document and generated
client. The original release console stages the prepared source and service
together. Use that console to review changed data mappings or prices, activate
the next version, restart the child and roll back to the retained previous
version. The credential environment stays with the original operating host.

## Complete an isolated provider operation

The original `native-journey.mjs` supports both the native Redis server and
Upstash. Its Upstash mode requires a dedicated ephemeral database because it
writes its own demonstration inputs. The operator supplies that newly created
database's endpoint and standard token; an optional
`UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_READ_TOKEN` selects a separate merchant read credential.

Upstash publishes an explicitly free, 72-hour
[agent database endpoint](https://upstash.com/blog/redis-database-for-agents).
Retain its returned credentials privately with this one operation. Use an
existing installed Starforge source and the original native payment peers:

```sh
export SF30_REDIS_JOURNEY_PROVIDER=upstash-rest
export SF30_UPSTASH_JOURNEY_ALLOW_SEED=owned-ephemeral-database
export SF30_REDIS_JOURNEY_OUTPUT=/srv/operations/upstash-native-result.json
node /srv/starforge/source/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/redis/native-journey.mjs
```

The source and all customer reads use a fresh random key namespace. The operation
checks authentication and the provider's read-only Lua behavior, seeds real
binary/hash/rank/stream records, serves the original paid products, reopens six
saved buyer responses, changes source and price, removes the authoring folder,
then completes native child upgrade and rollback. Its facilitator remains the
original local protocol fixture. Successful completion deletes the operation's
seed keys and retains the complete result at the requested output path.

Keep the installed source, dependency lock and original output with the delivery.
The ordinary Redis mode retains its existing server, authenticated database 2
and native ACL operation.

# Redis / Valkey merchant

Publish reviewed Redis records as paid HTTP products through the original SF30
seller. A private source declares the connection, fixed keys, typed inputs,
projected fields and execution limits. A merchant plan supplies the public
routes, examples and exact native payment alternatives. Preparation creates the
original seller service, OpenAPI document and generated buyer client together.

The source supports Redis 7 or later and Valkey 7.2 or later with `EVAL_RO`.
Native profiles select standalone Redis, Redis Cluster or Redis Sentinel. They
use the maintained `@redis/client` 6.2.1 implementation and the existing SF30
developer portal, operations interface and request lifecycle.

## Connect an Upstash source

The same merchant supports Upstash's native HTTPS/RESP2 transport. Start with
`starforge redis init --directory NEW_DIRECTORY --transport upstash-rest`.
The [Upstash customer guide](UPSTASH.md) covers credentials, original-source
preflight, customer preparation, retained releases and the complete native
provider operation. The existing read-only query engine and exact value handling
are shared by both connection types.

## Install the native feature

Select a distribution archive that includes the Redis command and its runtime
dependency manifest. Use that archive's published SHA-256 in place of
`ARCHIVE_SHA256` below. The maintained installer prepares the original native
payment SDK and the Redis driver together:

```sh
starforge runtime-install prepare --dir /srv/starforge/redis-runtime \
  --archive /srv/releases/starforge.tgz --sha256 ARCHIVE_SHA256 \
  --native --feature redis --operator
starforge runtime-install install --dir /srv/starforge/redis-runtime
starforge runtime-install inspect --dir /srv/starforge/redis-runtime --load --source
```

`--operator` checks the existing Linux release and host requirements, including
Python 3.11 or later and `flock`. The package source remains under
`/srv/starforge/redis-runtime/package/source`, and the selected dependencies live
under `/srv/starforge/redis-runtime/node_modules`. Run the original command from
that installed source:

```sh
starforge runtime-install run --dir /srv/starforge/redis-runtime -- \
  doctor --native --feature redis
```

For the remaining examples, replace the `starforge` prefix with
`starforge runtime-install run --dir /srv/starforge/redis-runtime --` when using
this retained runtime. The original [runtime installation guide](../../distribution/RUNTIME_INSTALL.md)
also covers upgrades and recovery. `doctor --feature redis` checks the declared
driver import, and `--native` includes the native SDK dependencies.

## Start from the supplied examples

```sh
mkdir -p /srv/merchant
starforge redis init --directory /srv/merchant/redis
starforge redis describe --source /srv/merchant/redis/source.json
```

`init` creates source, plan and input files in a new private directory. Edit the
connection and map the example keys to the existing merchant data. All supplied
query inputs have defaults, so the initial `input.json` is `{}`. Replace the
example public origin, asset and recipient with the merchant's reviewed payment
terms before starting native payment mode. Then inspect the live source and
prepare the merchant:

```sh
starforge redis preflight --source /srv/merchant/redis/source.json
starforge redis query --source /srv/merchant/redis/source.json \
  --query catalog --input /srv/merchant/redis/input.json
starforge redis prepare --source /srv/merchant/redis/source.json \
  --plan /srv/merchant/redis/merchant-plan.json \
  --directory /srv/merchant/redis/packages-first
starforge redis verify --directory /srv/merchant/redis/packages-first
starforge redis start --directory /srv/merchant/redis/packages-first \
  --port 8423 --operations-port 8424
```

`describe` and its `inspect` alias show public query contracts offline.
`preflight` opens the configured source and returns its native inspection and
current connection status. `query` reads one named product directly and closes
its owned source afterward. Add `--output NEW_FILE` to retain the complete JSON
result in a create-only private file.

Omitting `--facilitator` starts the seller in `CHALLENGE_ONLY` mode. Native
payment mode uses the existing explicit facilitator configuration. Use Ctrl-C
to stop a foreground run; the seller drains before closing its source.

```sh
starforge redis start --directory /srv/merchant/redis/packages-first \
  --facilitator https://facilitator.example --port 8423 --operations-port 8424
```

The printed result includes the actual seller URL, developer documentation,
OpenAPI and operations URLs. `run` is an alias for `start`. To operate an already
reviewed source and service directly, use `serve --source source.json --config
service.json` with the same launch options. Source-checkout users can replace
`starforge redis` with `node
stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/redis/cli.mjs`.

## Declare the product

The source schema is `stellar-forge.redis-source.v1`. Each named product uses one
of four native read shapes:

| Kind | Selection and public result |
| --- | --- |
| `get` | One declared string key and one public column |
| `hash` | One key and an explicit public-column to Redis-field mapping |
| `sorted-set` | One key, ordered member and score columns, and optional rank-offset input |
| `stream` | One key, stream ID plus explicitly projected fields, and optional exclusive-ID input |

Keys are either fixed literal strings or `{ "prefix": "merchant:catalog:",
"parameter": "region" }`. A key parameter must be a declared string with an
explicit enum. The examples permit the reviewed `north` and `south` catalog
keys. Public descriptions include parameter contracts, columns, kinds and
limits; the private source retains the actual keys and Redis field names.

The source shares the seller's scalar declaration compiler. Redis inputs use
non-null strings and signed 64-bit integer values. Strings must be well-formed
Unicode and reject NUL. Integer
JSON numbers must be safe integers; decimal integer strings retain the full
supported range. Every declared input has a purpose in key selection or paging.
Defaults, enums and declared bounds are applied before native execution.

For a sorted set, `offset` names an integer parameter with an inclusive minimum
of at least zero and maximum at most 10,000,000. For a stream, `after` names a
string parameter with `maxLength` at most 41. Its value is `-` for the first page
or a canonical `milliseconds-sequence` ID with two unsigned 64-bit components.
The stream selection begins strictly after that ID.

The plan schema is `stellar-forge.redis-merchant-plan.v1`. Every public route
selects a configured query and supplies method, path, service name, description,
parameter descriptions, example and payment terms. The shared public compiler
checks both the original example and its actual HTTP representation using the
Redis binder. The example plan contains four ready-to-edit routes matching the
four product kinds.

## Read pages and preserve values

Results provide the declared columns, rows, row count and truncation state.
Redis text, stream IDs and score replies remain strings. Missing values use JSON
null. Binary values that are not valid UTF-8 use a `{ "base64": "..." }` object.
Redis sorted-set numeric representation and ordering continue to apply to score
values; the reader preserves their native textual reply.

When a stream entry repeats a field name, its projection uses that entry's last
value for the field. Stream results expose
`duplicateFieldProjection: "last-value"` with the returned rows.

Each request runs the fixed read-only projection script once. Projection and
native byte accounting happen inside Redis before selected values are returned
to the client. The declared `maxRows` is 1 for string and hash products and up to
1,000 for paged products. `maxBytes` is 1,024–917,504 bytes, and `timeoutMs` is
50–30,000 milliseconds. The complete JSON response also remains within the
selected byte limit. A result that exceeds either byte check returns
`QUERY_RESULT_TOO_LARGE`; the HTTP route uses status 413. Adjust the reviewed
projection or page size, or the declared byte limit, before requesting it again.

Declare `offset` or `after` to expose continuation for a paged product. Use the
returned `nextInput` as the next request's input. It retains the current
key-selection values and advances the declared
rank or stream cursor. A continuation is emitted only when it passes the same
input contract as a new request. If the next rank exceeds the declared offset
maximum, the response reports `continuationUnavailable: "OFFSET_LIMIT"`. A
cursor excluded by an enum or another declared input constraint reports
`continuationUnavailable: "INPUT_LIMIT"`. In either case `truncated` may still
be true because more source rows exist. The merchant can revise the reviewed
declaration to expose a wider range.

Each page is an individual live read. Changes to a sorted
set between requests can change rank positions; the stream cursor follows
native stream IDs. Release retention pins the reader configuration, while the
Redis dataset continues under its own operational lifecycle.

## Configure the native connection

The private `connection` selects one deployment. Omitted `topology` keeps the
original standalone profile. All native profiles accept `username`,
`passwordEnv`, `tls` and `caFile`. The host environment supplies the password
when a preview or seller starts. TLS defaults to `verify-full`, which validates
the server certificate and hostname. An explicit CA is relative to the source
file and is copied into prepared packages and retained releases.

| Deployment | Required connection fields | Database |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Standalone | `host`; optional `port` defaults to 6379 | `database` defaults to 0 |
| Cluster | `topology: "cluster"`, `rootNodes` | Database 0 |
| Sentinel | `topology: "sentinel"`, `name`, `sentinelRootNodes` | `database` defaults to 0 on the data server |

Start from the corresponding complete source and merchant-plan templates:

```sh
starforge redis init --directory /srv/merchant/cluster --topology cluster
starforge redis init --directory /srv/merchant/sentinel --topology sentinel
```

Each seed list contains 1–16 distinct `{ "host": "...", "port": 6379 }`
endpoints. Cluster seeds default to port 6379; Sentinel seeds default to 26379.
Use several independently reachable seeds so the driver can discover the
deployment when one seed is unavailable. `describe` reports the topology and
seed count without exposing hosts or credential values.

### Cluster

A Cluster connection uses the same merchant credentials and TLS settings for
seed discovery and every discovered data node:

```json
{
  "topology": "cluster",
  "rootNodes": [
    { "host": "redis-1.example", "port": 6379 },
    { "host": "redis-2.example", "port": 6379 },
    { "host": "redis-3.example", "port": 6379 }
  ],
  "username": "merchant",
  "passwordEnv": "REDIS_MERCHANT_PASSWORD",
  "tls": "verify-full"
}
```

Every declared product reads one selected Redis key. The driver receives that
key with the original `EVAL_RO` invocation, routes it to the slot's primary and
handles native `MOVED` and `ASK` redirects. The reader uses primary nodes.
Different products and enum-selected keys can occupy different slots. A Cluster
profile rejects nonzero databases before opening a connection.

### Sentinel

A Sentinel profile names the monitored primary and separates discovery
credentials and TLS from data credentials and TLS:

```json
{
  "topology": "sentinel",
  "name": "merchant-primary",
  "sentinelRootNodes": [
    { "host": "sentinel-1.example", "port": 26379 },
    { "host": "sentinel-2.example", "port": 26379 },
    { "host": "sentinel-3.example", "port": 26379 }
  ],
  "database": 0,
  "username": "merchant",
  "passwordEnv": "REDIS_MERCHANT_PASSWORD",
  "tls": "verify-full",
  "sentinelUsername": "merchant-monitor",
  "sentinelPasswordEnv": "REDIS_SENTINEL_PASSWORD",
  "sentinelTls": "verify-full"
}
```

`sentinelTls` also defaults to `verify-full`. Set `caFile` for a private
data-server CA and `sentinelCaFile` for a private Sentinel CA. Preparation
retains them independently as `database-ca.pem` and `sentinel-ca.pem` and
lists both required environment names in the manifest. The saved workspace
retains the original certificate bytes and environment references through
reopen, customer preparation and release staging.

The native Sentinel client discovers and reads the current primary. Its
existing topology refresh handles a promoted primary; this reader does not
select replicas. Supply monitor credentials for the Sentinel service and data
credentials for the database nodes. Configure each service through its own
existing administration interface.

### Advertised addresses and local receiving

Cluster and Sentinel deployments may advertise addresses that differ from the
host's reachable addresses. An optional `nodeAddressMap` translates exact
advertised `host:port` strings to explicit endpoints:

```json
{
  "nodeAddressMap": {
    "10.20.0.12:6379": { "host": "redis-2.internal.example", "port": 6379 }
  }
}
```

The map permits at most 256 entries. Each destination specifies its port.
Sentinel applies the same map to discovered monitor and data endpoints. Keep the
mapped endpoint compatible with its server certificate and the host's existing
network access.

For a local development deployment, explicitly choose `local-plaintext`.
If either the data or Sentinel connection uses this mode, every seed, mapped
endpoint and discovered destination must be `127.0.0.1`, `::1` or
`localhost`. The source checks discovered destinations as well as the initial
profile. Use the verified TLS profiles for a remote deployment.

### Connection lifetime

The source has explicit `maxConnections`, `maxPending`, `connectTimeoutMs`,
`idleTimeoutMs` and `startupTimeoutMs`. For Cluster and Sentinel,
`maxConnections` counts owned logical clients; the native driver opens the
sockets needed for discovery and data nodes inside each client. Size this limit
alongside the deployment's socket capacity. The default is four logical clients.

The source reuses ready clients and keeps requests within the configured queue
and lifetime. On cancellation or deadline it retires the affected client and
joins its connection and command work before releasing its pool slot. Closing
the source joins all retiring clients as well as active work. A failed seed can
fall through to another configured seed using the native driver.

A client deadline ends the reader's request; a script already executing on
Redis continues according to the server's script lifecycle. Stopping a seller
uses the existing HTTP drain before closing its source.

## Grant the command and key permissions

The merchant identity needs `+eval_ro` and `+ping`, plus the commands used by its
declared products: `+get`, `+strlen`, `+hmget`, `+hstrlen`, `+zrange`, and
`+xrange`. Selecting a nonzero database also requires `+select`. Restrict its key
permissions to the fixed merchant keys represented by the source declarations.

For an existing dedicated merchant user whose password is already configured,
the example source uses this ACL permission fragment:

```text
ACL SETUSER merchant on resetkeys -@all ~merchant:availability:catalog ~merchant:catalog:north ~merchant:catalog:south ~merchant:rankings:daily ~merchant:events +eval_ro +ping +get +strlen +hmget +hstrlen +zrange +xrange
```

For Cluster, add `+cluster|slots` for native discovery and `+asking` for a
read redirected during a slot migration. Apply the merchant identity and its
key permissions consistently to the Cluster's data nodes.

For Sentinel, configure the separate monitor reader with `+ping`,
`+sentinel|master`, `+sentinel|replicas`, `+sentinel|sentinels`,
`+psubscribe` and `+punsubscribe`, together with channel access for native
topology notifications. The integration fixture uses `&*` for that monitor
identity. The data-server merchant retains the read permissions above. Sentinel
administration and failover use the deployment's existing administrator identity.

Apply the equivalent settings through the database's existing administration
interface. Native script execution respects the user's command and key
permissions. Redis-compatible hosted providers must expose the same read-only
script capability for this source.

Primary command and access-control references:

- [Redis EVAL_RO](https://redis.io/docs/latest/commands/eval_ro/)
- [Valkey EVAL_RO](https://valkey.io/commands/eval_ro/)
- [Redis ACL](https://redis.io/docs/latest/operate/oss_and_stack/management/security/acl/)
- [node-redis 6.2.1 Cluster](https://github.com/redis/node-redis/blob/redis%406.2.1/docs/clustering.md)
- [node-redis 6.2.1 Sentinel](https://github.com/redis/node-redis/blob/redis%406.2.1/docs/sentinel.md)

## Operate the service and retained releases

`start` and `serve` accept `--max-in-flight`, `--drain-grace-ms`, and
`--availability-dir` for the existing seller controls. `--no-operations` runs
only the seller listener. An explicitly selected loopback HTTP facilitator uses
`--allow-local-facilitator`; normal facilitator URLs use HTTPS.

The same prepared package can be retained, compared, activated and rolled back
through `starforge releases stage --redis-package PREPARED_DIRECTORY`. The
existing release console operates the actual retained source and original
seller. See [Redis releases](../../sf82-seller-pilot/REDIS_RELEASES.md) for the
complete package-to-release workflow.

The retained generated client includes its original `client-export.json`
manifest alongside the JavaScript, TypeScript, OpenAPI, package and README
files. Preparation hashes all six client files, and release staging carries
them together for the original client inspection and download flow.

Embedded consumers can use `openRedisSourceFile`, `prepareRedisSeller`,
`verifyPreparedRedisSeller`, `startRedisSeller`, `bindRedisSeller` and
`createRedisNativeFactory`. The source owns Redis queries and connection
lifetime; the existing SF30 seller and SF82 manager own payment, service and
release operation.

## Native integration journey

Run `node native-journey.mjs` from this directory after installing the selected
native runtime. `REDIS_SERVER` selects an installed Redis 7+ executable; its
shared libraries must already be available to the process. The journey creates
an isolated loopback Redis database, exercises the four read products through
an ACL user, exports the original customer client, and uses the original buyer
and SF82 child process for upgrade and rollback. Its facilitator is the existing
local x402 protocol fixture. `SF30_REDIS_JOURNEY_OUTPUT` optionally saves the
result to a selected file.

Set `SF30_REDIS_JOURNEY_TOPOLOGY=cluster` for three native primaries, live slot
routing and a slot migration, or `SF30_REDIS_JOURNEY_TOPOLOGY=sentinel` for an
authenticated primary/replica deployment and three Sentinel monitors with an
actual primary promotion. These modes continue through the same declared
products, merchant, buyer, customer files and retained release journey. Add
`SF30_REDIS_JOURNEY_WORKSPACE=1` and `SF30_REDIS_WORKSPACE_BROWSER=1` to include
the existing saved editor and browser flow on the selected deployment. The
native journey owns and closes the ephemeral Redis processes it starts.

Add `SF30_REDIS_JOURNEY_TLS=1` to the Sentinel run to generate separate data
and monitor CAs and real SAN certificates through the installed `openssl`
executable. That run uses verified TLS on both planes, retains both CA files
through the original workspace and package, removes the original merchant CA
source copies, and continues through the retained seller's actual customer
deliveries and release changes. The selected Redis executable must include TLS.

The integrated run on Redis 7.0.15 and `@redis/client` 6.2.1 completed six buyer
deliveries, retained every original response file, and restored the original
ranking result after rollback. It also exercised authenticated database
selection, binary values, exact decimal text, missing projected fields, stream
duplicate fields, pagination boundaries, and both native and encoded result
size limits.

## Saved authoring workspace

The [Redis merchant workspace](workspace/README.md) combines named-product editing, complete saved revisions, live source previews, original customer packages and retained release controls. Use `starforge-merchant redis workspace create --directory NEW --source SOURCE --plan PLAN`, then `starforge-merchant redis workspace open --directory WORKSPACE`. The browser and CLI share the same private workspace; the host-selected connection and environment credential references carry through to the original merchant.

// MIT. One fixed Redis/Valkey EVAL_RO script. Buyers supply typed values, never code.
// Projection and byte accounting happen before any database value crosses the wire.
export const READ_SCRIPT = `
local kind, count, budget, position = ARGV[1], tonumber(ARGV[2]), tonumber(ARGV[3]), ARGV[4]
local rows, used, truncated = {}, 0, 0
local function keep(value)
  if type(value) == 'string' then
    used = used + string.len(value)
    if used > budget then error('SF30_RESULT_TOO_LARGE') end
  end
  return value
end
if kind == 'get' then
  if redis.call('STRLEN', KEYS[1]) > budget then error('SF30_RESULT_TOO_LARGE') end
  rows[1] = {keep(redis.call('GET', KEYS[1]))}
elseif kind == 'hash' then
  local size, fields = 0, {}
  for i = 5, #ARGV do
    size = size + redis.call('HSTRLEN', KEYS[1], ARGV[i])
    if size > budget then error('SF30_RESULT_TOO_LARGE') end
    fields[#fields + 1] = ARGV[i]
  end
  local values = redis.call('HMGET', KEYS[1], unpack(fields))
  for i = 1, #values do keep(values[i]) end
  rows[1] = values
elseif kind == 'sorted-set' then
  local start = tonumber(position)
  for offset = start, start + count do
    local pair = redis.call('ZRANGE', KEYS[1], tostring(offset), tostring(offset), 'WITHSCORES')
    if #pair == 0 then break end
    if offset == start + count then truncated = 1; break end
    rows[#rows + 1] = {keep(pair[1]), keep(pair[2])}
  end
elseif kind == 'stream' then
  local cursor = position == '-' and '-' or '(' .. position
  for i = 1, count + 1 do
    local entries = redis.call('XRANGE', KEYS[1], cursor, '+', 'COUNT', 1)
    if #entries == 0 then break end
    if i > count then truncated = 1; break end
    local entry, selected = entries[1], {}
    for j = 1, #entry[2], 2 do selected[entry[2][j]] = entry[2][j + 1] end
    local row = {keep(entry[1])}
    for j = 5, #ARGV do row[#row + 1] = keep(selected[ARGV[j]] or false) end
    rows[#rows + 1] = row
    cursor = '(' .. entry[1]
  end
else error('SF30_QUERY_KIND_INVALID') end
return {truncated, rows}
`;

# Redis merchant workspace

Create and operate named Redis or Valkey data products from one saved workspace. The editor supports native standalone, Cluster and Sentinel deployments and Upstash HTTPS source profiles. It uses the original Redis query compiler and live source, original merchant preparer and generated client, and the original retained seller release store.

## Open an existing source as a workspace

Use Node 22.16 or later. The host selects the source connection and its environment references. For native TCP, install the Redis feature through the merchant runtime; the Upstash transport uses Node's HTTPS implementation. Importing and editing a workspace is offline. Live previews require the configured database and credentials.

```sh
starforge-merchant redis workspace create \
  --directory /private/redis-workspace \
  --source /private/redis-source.json \
  --plan /private/merchant-plan.json \
```

## Continue after interruption

One original private-directory writer owns the workspace. SQLite commits save revisions, head changes and operation outcomes. The source and plan materializations are regenerated atomically from saved revisions; a partial write does not prevent the same operation from continuing.

After an interrupted process, reopen the same directory and inspect the saved operation. `resume --id REQUEST_ID` continues its exact input. A completed revision, prepared package or staged release is read and reconciled before the operation completes. Partial original packages are retained under the workspace's `interrupted` directory before a new original preparation attempt. Each resumed attempt remains on the same operation record.

The browser offers the same request retrieval and continuation. A lost response keeps the original pending request in browser storage. Refresh retrieves its original result; Continue sends that exact request or resumes its interrupted server record.

## Export and receive

Use the maintained Starforge command with the seller's original developer

```sh
starforge client python export --openapi seller-openapi.json --out ./customer
starforge client python status --dir ./customer
```

## Prepare a source-bound request

Run from this customer directory, or import its module from your application:

```python
from pathlib import Path
from seller_client import SellerClient
from stellar_forge_buyer import Buyer

api = SellerClient()  # Uses the package beside seller_client.py.
print(api.source)
for operation in api.operations:
    print(operation['id'], operation['method'], operation['path'])

request = api.build_request(
    operation_id=selected_operation_id,  # An actual ID printed above.
    inputs=reviewed_inputs,
    intent_id='customer-report-2026-10-11',
    accept_index=0,                     # An explicit original payment choice.
    max_atomic='25000',                 # Your explicit ceiling, not auto-price.
)
request.save(Path('./private-request'))
print(request.describe())               # Complete terms and body digest.
```

Inputs follow the original JavaScript client's contract: `path`, `query`, and a
JSON `body` where the operation requires it. Query values are strings or lists of
strings. Use `omitBody: True` only for a declared optional body. A retained
multipart body is `{'multipart': {'body': exact_bytes, 'contentType': exact_type}}`;
keep the original multipart boundary. Python rejects non-finite numbers, cycles,
non-string dictionary keys and integers outside JavaScript's exact integer range
rather than silently rounding them. Atomic payment amounts stay decimal strings,
including values above 2**53. Actual seller validation remains authoritative.

The default payment flow is `authorization`. Only for a selected original offer
that explicitly advertises it, pass `payment_flow='upfront'`. Upfront settlement
can precede application generation; delivery failure may still leave a charge.
URL, method, network, asset, recipient and timeout cannot be overridden by this
adapter. Multiple advertised payment options require an explicit selection.

```python
buyer = Buyer(
```

`prepare` creates an original native operation and calls its normal offline
review. It does not execute a purchase. The returned object is the original
`Operation`; its configuration, response-stream options, execution, dataset/file
results, accounting, recovery and export APIs remain available unchanged.
This adapter does not create an alternate ledger, signer, HTTP client or retry.
A saved source price never authorizes a purchase by itself. Native SF88 requires
its supported public HTTPS resources even when an exported development client
can build an original loopback request.

## Reopen without repeating a purchase

```python
api = SellerClient('./receiving-copy')
buyer = Buyer(checkout=native_source, state_dir=original_state_directory)
operation = api.reopen(buyer, 'customer-report-2026-10-11')
result = operation.recover()  # Original recorded outcome; does not purchase again.
```

The client checks the same source, operation ID, exact request and body before
returning the original operation. Configure changes to trusted operator paths
and response settings remain usable. Changing the operation URL, body, headers
or spend terms requires preparing and reviewing the intended new request.

For a process interruption or lost reply **during preparation**, reload the
saved request and explicitly call `api.resume_preparation(buyer, request)`.
This inspects the already existing operation, verifies its full request and body
and repeats only the original offline review. It does not create or execute an
operation. It completes a missing source sidecar only for an unattempted matching
preparation. An attempted operation without that sidecar stays with the original
buyer's recovery tools rather than being assigned to a new client source.

A request-plan save interrupted partway through can be completed by saving the
same `BoundRequest` to the same directory. Completed files must match exactly.
Loading a plan verifies its files and reconstructs the request with the original
builder, so a consistently edited metadata file cannot redirect a saved request.
Keep request plans and buyer state private: they may contain customer payloads.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Receive an exact Git source cache from captured GitData and existing sources.
MIT. The maintained builder remains the package/profile/runtime authority.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import argparse
import datetime as dt
import fcntl
import hashlib
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path, PurePosixPath
import re
import stat
import subprocess
import sys
import threading
import uuid
import zlib

SCHEMA = "stellar-forge.git-object-receiving.v1"
STATE_SCHEMA = "stellar-forge.git-object-cache.v1"
OID = re.compile(r"^[a-f0-9]{40}$")
FILE_LIMIT = 2 * 1024 * 1024
SOURCE_LIMIT = 64 * 1024 * 1024
METADATA_LIMIT = 8 * 1024 * 1024

class SourceError(Exception):
    pass

def need(value, message):
    if not value:
        raise SourceError(message)

def now():
    return dt.datetime.now(dt.timezone.utc).isoformat()

def object_id(kind, data):
    return hashlib.sha1(f"{kind} {len(data)}\0".encode("ascii") + data).hexdigest()

def canonical(value):
    return (json.dumps(value, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False) + "\n").encode("utf-8")

def regular(path, maximum=FILE_LIMIT):
    fd = os.open(path, os.O_RDONLY | os.O_NOFOLLOW)
    try:
        before = os.fstat(fd)
        need(stat.S_ISREG(before.st_mode) and before.st_size <= maximum, "Expected a bounded regular source file")
        with os.fdopen(fd, "rb", closefd=False) as handle:
            data = handle.read(maximum + 1)
        after = os.fstat(fd)
        need(len(data) == before.st_size and (before.st_dev, before.st_ino, before.st_size, before.st_mtime_ns) ==
             (after.st_dev, after.st_ino, after.st_size, after.st_mtime_ns), "Source file changed during reading")
        return data
    finally:
        os.close(fd)

def absolute_directory(value, exists=True):
    path = Path(value)
    need(path.is_absolute() and str(path) == str(path.absolute()), "Use an absolute source/cache directory")
    need(path.resolve(strict=exists) == path, "Source/cache directories must retain their canonical path")
    if exists:
        need(stat.S_ISDIR(path.lstat().st_mode), "Expected an existing source/cache directory")
    return path

def json_file(path, maximum=METADATA_LIMIT):
    data = regular(path, maximum)
    if data.startswith(b"\x1f\x8b"):
        decoder = zlib.decompressobj(31)
        data = decoder.decompress(data, maximum + 1)
        need(len(data) <= maximum and decoder.eof and not decoder.unused_data and not decoder.unconsumed_tail,
             "Compressed source metadata exceeds its original bounded size")
    return json.loads(data)

def atomic_json(path, value):
    data = canonical(value)
    temporary = path.with_name(path.name + "." + uuid.uuid4().hex + ".receiving-tmp")
    fd = os.open(temporary, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL | os.O_NOFOLLOW, 0o600)
    try:
        with os.fdopen(fd, "wb", closefd=False) as handle:
            handle.write(data)
            handle.flush()
            os.fsync(handle.fileno())
    finally:
        os.close(fd)
    os.replace(temporary, path)

def validate_metadata(value):
    need(isinstance(value, dict) and value.get("schema") == SCHEMA, "Unsupported Git source receiving schema")
    source = value.get("source")
    tree = value.get("tree")
    commit_text = value.get("commitText")
    need(isinstance(source, dict) and OID.fullmatch(source.get("commit", "")) and
         OID.fullmatch(source.get("tree", "")), "Exact original commit and root tree IDs are required")
    need(isinstance(tree, dict) and tree.get("sha") == source["tree"] and tree.get("truncated") is False and
         isinstance(tree.get("tree"), list), "The complete original recursive tree is required")
    need(isinstance(commit_text, str), "Original commit bytes are required as UTF-8 commitText")
    commit = commit_text.encode("utf-8")
    need(object_id("commit", commit) == source["commit"], "Original Git commit object hash does not match")
    need(commit_text.split("\n", 1)[0] == "tree " + source["tree"], "Commit and recursive root tree differ")
    entries = {}
    groups = {"": []}
    expected_trees = {"": source["tree"]}
    for row in tree["tree"]:
        need(isinstance(row, dict), "Invalid recursive tree row")
        path, mode, kind, oid = (row.get(k) for k in ("path", "mode", "type", "sha"))
        need(isinstance(path, str) and path and "\0" not in path and not path.startswith("/") and
             all(part not in ("", ".", "..") for part in path.split("/")), "Invalid original Git path")
        need(path not in entries and OID.fullmatch(oid or ""), "Duplicate path or invalid original object ID")
        need((kind, mode) in (("tree", "040000"), ("blob", "100644"), ("blob", "100755"),
                              ("blob", "120000"), ("commit", "160000")), "Unsupported original Git tree mode/type")
        entries[path] = row
        parent, _, name = path.rpartition("/")
        groups.setdefault(parent, []).append((name, row))
        if kind == "tree":
            expected_trees[path] = oid
            groups.setdefault(path, [])
    need(set(groups) == set(expected_trees), "Recursive tree omits an intermediate tree")
    objects = []
    for path, rows in groups.items():
        rows.sort(key=lambda item: (item[0] + ("/" if item[1]["type"] == "tree" else "")).encode("utf-8"))
        body = b"".join(
            (row["mode"].lstrip("0") + " " + name).encode("utf-8") + b"\0" + bytes.fromhex(row["sha"])
            for name, row in rows
        )
        need(object_id("tree", body) == expected_trees[path], "Original Git tree object hash does not match: " + path)
        objects.append((expected_trees[path], "tree", body))
    required = value.get("requiredPaths")
    need(isinstance(required, list) and required and len(required) == len(set(required)),
         "Original required source paths must be a nonempty unique list")
    selected = []
    for path in required:
        row = entries.get(path)
        need(row and row["type"] == "blob" and row["mode"] in ("100644", "100755"),
             "Only an original regular source path can be received: " + str(path))
        need(isinstance(row.get("size"), int) and 0 <= row["size"] <= FILE_LIMIT, "Source file exceeds its original limit")
        selected.append(row)
    need(sum(row["size"] for row in selected) <= SOURCE_LIMIT, "Required source exceeds the maintained 64 MiB budget")
    objects.append((source["commit"], "commit", commit))
    return source, entries, selected, objects

def git_command(git, repository, args, **options):
    environment = dict(os.environ, GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT="0")
    return subprocess.run(
        [git, "--no-replace-objects", "--no-lazy-fetch", "-C", str(repository), *args],
        shell=False, env=environment, **options
    )

class ObjectCache:
    def __init__(self, repository):
        self.repository = repository
        self.written = 0
        self.raw_bytes = 0

    def path(self, oid):
        need(OID.fullmatch(oid) is not None, "Invalid Git object ID")
        return self.repository / "objects" / oid[:2] / oid[2:]

    def read(self, oid, expected_kind=None):
        path = self.path(oid)
        if not path.exists():
            return None
        compressed = regular(path, FILE_LIMIT + 1024 * 1024)
        decoder = zlib.decompressobj()
        raw = decoder.decompress(compressed, FILE_LIMIT + 1024 * 1024)
        need(decoder.eof and not decoder.unused_data and not decoder.unconsumed_tail, "Git object exceeds its bounded original size")
        head, body = raw.split(b"\0", 1)
        kind, size = head.decode("ascii").split(" ")
        need(size == str(len(body)) and object_id(kind, body) == oid, "Cached original Git object changed")
        need(expected_kind is None or kind == expected_kind, "Cached Git object has the wrong type")
        return body

    def write(self, oid, kind, body):
        need(object_id(kind, body) == oid, "Received bytes do not match the original Git object")
        path = self.path(oid)
        path.parent.mkdir(mode=0o700, exist_ok=True)
        if path.exists():
            need(self.read(oid, kind) == body, "Existing immutable Git object differs")
            return False
        raw = f"{kind} {len(body)}\0".encode("ascii") + body
        compressed = zlib.compress(raw)
        temporary = path.parent / ("tmp_obj_" + uuid.uuid4().hex + ".receiving")
        fd = os.open(temporary, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL | os.O_NOFOLLOW, 0o600)
        try:
            with os.fdopen(fd, "wb", closefd=False) as handle:
                handle.write(compressed)
                handle.flush()
                os.fsync(handle.fileno())
            try:
                os.link(temporary, path, follow_symlinks=False)
            except FileExistsError:
                need(self.read(oid, kind) == body, "Concurrent immutable Git object differs")
                return False
        finally:
            os.close(fd)
            temporary.unlink(missing_ok=True)
        self.written += 1
        self.raw_bytes += len(body)
        return True

def receive_git_donor(git, donor, cache, missing):
    """Read batches from an existing object database; never fetch or alter it."""
    ids = list(missing)
    if not ids:
        return 0
    inspected = git_command(git, donor, ["cat-file", "--batch-check"],
                            input=("\n".join(ids) + "\n").encode("ascii"),
                            stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, timeout=60)
    need(inspected.returncode == 0, "Existing Git donor metadata read failed (exit " + str(inspected.returncode) + ")")
    lines = inspected.stdout.decode("ascii").splitlines()
    need(len(lines) == len(ids), "Incomplete original Git donor metadata batch")
    available = []
    for oid, line in zip(ids, lines):
        fields = line.split(" ")
        need(fields[0] == oid, "Original Git donor metadata order changed")
        if fields[1:] == ["missing"]:
            continue
        need(len(fields) == 3 and fields[1] == "blob" and int(fields[2]) == missing[oid]["size"],
             "Original Git donor object metadata differs")
        available.append(oid)
    if not available:
        return 0
    environment = dict(os.environ, GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT="0")
    process = subprocess.Popen(
        [git, "--no-replace-objects", "--no-lazy-fetch", "-C", str(donor), "cat-file", "--batch"],
        stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL, env=environment, shell=False
    )
    send_error = []
    def send():
        try:
            process.stdin.write(("\n".join(available) + "\n").encode("ascii"))
            process.stdin.close()
        except BaseException as error:
            send_error.append(type(error).__name__)
    sender = threading.Thread(target=send, daemon=True)
    sender.start()
    received = 0
    try:
        for oid in available:
            header = process.stdout.readline(160).decode("ascii").rstrip("\n").split(" ")
            need(len(header) == 3 and header[0] == oid and header[1] == "blob" and
                 int(header[2]) == missing[oid]["size"], "Original donor content header changed")
            size = int(header[2])
            body = process.stdout.read(size)
            need(len(body) == size and process.stdout.read(1) == b"\n", "Original donor content was truncated")
            cache.write(oid, "blob", body)
            del missing[oid]
            received += 1
        need(process.stdout.read(1) == b"", "Unexpected extra original donor content")
        sender.join(timeout=10)
        need(not sender.is_alive() and not send_error and process.wait(timeout=10) == 0, "Original donor batch did not finish")
        return received
    finally:
        if process.poll() is None:
            process.terminate()
            try:
                process.wait(timeout=10)
            except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
                process.kill()
                process.wait(timeout=10)
        process.stdout.close()
        if not process.stdin.closed:
            process.stdin.close()

def receive_files(directory, selected, cache, missing, flat=False):
    received = 0
    for row in selected:
        oid = row["sha"]
        if oid not in missing:
            continue
        path = directory / (oid + ".blob") if flat else directory / row["path"]
        compressed_path = directory / (oid + ".blob.gz") if flat else None
        try:
            if compressed_path is not None and compressed_path.exists():
                packed = regular(compressed_path, FILE_LIMIT + 65536)
                decoder = zlib.decompressobj(31)
                data = decoder.decompress(packed, FILE_LIMIT + 1)
                need(len(data) <= FILE_LIMIT and decoder.eof and not decoder.unused_data and not decoder.unconsumed_tail,
                     "Received compressed blob exceeds its original source limit")
            else:
                data = regular(path)
        except FileNotFoundError:
            continue
        except OSError as error:
            if error.errno == 40:  # O_NOFOLLOW rejects source aliases.
                continue
            raise
        if len(data) != row["size"] or object_id("blob", data) != oid:
            continue
        cache.write(oid, "blob", data)
        del missing[oid]
        received += 1
    return received

def materialize(directory, selected, cache):
    directory = absolute_directory(directory, exists=False)
    directory.mkdir(mode=0o700, parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    materialized = 0
    for row in selected:
        data = cache.read(row["sha"], "blob")
        need(data is not None, "Receive the complete requested closure before materializing it")
        path = directory / row["path"]
        path.parent.mkdir(mode=0o700, parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        need(path.parent.resolve() == path.parent, "Materialized source directory was redirected")
        if path.exists():
            need(regular(path) == data, "Existing source postimage differs: " + row["path"])
            continue
        temporary = path.with_name(".receiving-" + uuid.uuid4().hex)
        fd = os.open(temporary, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL | os.O_NOFOLLOW,
                     0o755 if row["mode"] == "100755" else 0o644)
        try:
            with os.fdopen(fd, "wb", closefd=False) as handle:
                handle.write(data)
                handle.flush()
                os.fsync(handle.fileno())
            try:
                os.link(temporary, path, follow_symlinks=False)
            except FileExistsError:
                need(regular(path) == data, "Concurrent original source postimage differs")
        finally:
            os.close(fd)
            temporary.unlink(missing_ok=True)
        materialized += 1
    return materialized

def receive(args):
    metadata = json_file(Path(args.metadata))
    source, entries, selected, objects = validate_metadata(metadata)
    need(args.commit == source["commit"], "The explicit selected commit differs from the captured source")
    metadata_hash = hashlib.sha256(canonical(metadata)).hexdigest()
    directory = absolute_directory(args.directory, exists=False)
    directory.mkdir(mode=0o700, parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    lock = os.open(directory / "source-receiving.lock", os.O_RDWR | os.O_CREAT | os.O_NOFOLLOW, 0o600)
    try:
        fcntl.flock(lock, fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)
        state_file = directory / "source-receiving.json"
        previous = json_file(state_file) if state_file.exists() else None
        if previous:
            need(previous.get("schema") == STATE_SCHEMA and previous.get("directory") == str(directory) and
                 previous.get("source") == source and previous.get("metadataSha256") == metadata_hash,
                 "Resume the original cache with its exact original source metadata")
        else:
            need(not any(p.name != "source-receiving.lock" for p in directory.iterdir()),
                 "Create an owned cache directory or resume its original receiving record")
            previous = {"schema": STATE_SCHEMA, "directory": str(directory), "source": source,
                        "metadataSha256": metadata_hash, "createdAt": now(), "phase": "RECEIVING"}
            atomic_json(state_file, previous)
        repository = directory / "repository.git"
        if not repository.exists():
            started = subprocess.run([args.git, "init", "--bare", "--quiet", str(repository)],
                                     stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, shell=False, timeout=30)
            need(started.returncode == 0, "Could not initialize the owned Git object cache")
        additional = list(dict.fromkeys([*(previous.get("additionalPaths") or []), *args.additional_path]))
        selected_paths = {row["path"] for row in selected}
        for path in additional:
            row = entries.get(path)
            need(row and row["type"] == "blob" and row["mode"] in ("100644", "100755") and
                 isinstance(row.get("size"), int) and 0 <= row["size"] <= FILE_LIMIT,
                 "Additional closure path must be an original regular source file")
            if path not in selected_paths:
                selected.append(row)
                selected_paths.add(path)
        need(sum(row["size"] for row in selected) <= SOURCE_LIMIT, "Expanded source exceeds the maintained 64 MiB budget")
        cache = ObjectCache(repository)
        # Interrupted writes leave only our unreferenced temporary objects.
        for temporary in (repository / "objects").glob("??/tmp_obj_*.receiving"):
            need(stat.S_ISREG(temporary.lstat().st_mode), "Interrupted source temporary changed type")
            temporary.unlink()
        for oid, kind, body in objects:
            cache.write(oid, kind, body)
        # This is a shallow object cache for one immutable commit, with full tree
        # metadata and the requested native source blobs. Its parents remain exact.
        (repository / "shallow").write_text(source["commit"] + "\n", encoding="ascii")
        updated = git_command(args.git, repository, ["update-ref", "refs/heads/source", source["commit"]],
                              stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, timeout=30)
        need(updated.returncode == 0, "The owned Git cache requires Git with --no-lazy-fetch support")
        missing = {}
        for row in selected:
            if cache.read(row["sha"], "blob") is None:
                missing[row["sha"]] = {"sha": row["sha"], "size": row["size"], "paths": []}
        for row in selected:
            if row["sha"] in missing:
                missing[row["sha"]]["paths"].append(row["path"])
        donors = []
        for name in args.donor_repository:
            donor = absolute_directory(name)
            count = receive_git_donor(args.git, donor, cache, missing)
            donors.append({"kind": "original-git", "directory": str(donor), "objects": count})
        for name in args.donor_source:
            donor = absolute_directory(name)
            count = receive_files(donor, selected, cache, missing)
            donors.append({"kind": "original-source", "directory": str(donor), "objects": count})
        for name in args.incoming:
            donor = absolute_directory(name)
            count = receive_files(donor, selected, cache, missing, flat=True)
            donors.append({"kind": "received-blobs", "directory": str(donor), "objects": count})
        listed = git_command(args.git, repository, ["ls-tree", "-r", "-z", "--full-tree", source["commit"]],
                             stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, timeout=30)
        need(listed.returncode == 0, "Original Git could not enumerate the recovered source tree")
        actual = {}
        for line in listed.stdout.split(b"\0"):
            if not line:
                continue
            fields, path = line.split(b"\t", 1)
            mode, kind, oid = fields.decode("ascii").split(" ")
            actual[path.decode("utf-8")] = (mode, kind, oid)
        expected = {path: (row["mode"], row["type"], row["sha"])
                    for path, row in entries.items() if row["type"] != "tree"}
        need(actual == expected, "Git enumerated a different source tree")
        result = {**previous, "phase": "SOURCE_NEEDED" if missing else "OBJECTS_AVAILABLE",
                  "updatedAt": now(), "repository": str(repository), "gitTreeEntries": len(actual),
                  "verifiedTreeObjects": sum(kind == "tree" for _, kind, _ in objects),
                  "requiredPaths": len(selected), "requiredBytes": sum(row["size"] for row in selected),
                  "additionalPaths": additional,
                  "writtenObjects": cache.written, "writtenRawBytes": cache.raw_bytes, "donors": donors,
                  "missingObjects": len(missing), "missingBytes": sum(row["size"] for row in missing.values())}
        atomic_json(directory / "missing-objects.json", {"source": source, "objects": list(missing.values())})
        if args.materialize and not missing:
            result["materializedFiles"] = materialize(args.materialize, selected, cache)
            result["sourceDirectory"] = str(Path(args.materialize))
        atomic_json(state_file, result)
        print(json.dumps(result, separators=(",", ":")))
        return 2 if missing else 0
    finally:
        os.close(lock)

def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--metadata", required=True, help="Complete captured GitData tree and exact commitText")
    parser.add_argument("--commit", required=True, help="Explicit immutable original Git commit")
    parser.add_argument("--directory", required=True, help="New or original owned source-cache directory")
    parser.add_argument("--git", default="git", help="Existing Git executable with --no-lazy-fetch support")
    parser.add_argument("--donor-repository", action="append", default=[], help="Existing Git database, read only")
    parser.add_argument("--donor-source", action="append", default=[], help="Existing native source root, read only")
    parser.add_argument("--incoming", action="append", default=[], help="Exact received blobs named OID.blob or OID.blob.gz")
    parser.add_argument("--materialize", help="New native source directory for the complete requested closure")
    parser.add_argument("--additional-path", action="append", default=[], help="Exact source path subsequently requested by the maintained builder")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    try:
        return receive(args)
    except (SourceError, OSError, ValueError, zlib.error, subprocess.SubprocessError) as error:
        print(json.dumps({"phase": "ERROR", "code": type(error).__name__, "message": str(error)[:1200]}),
              file=sys.stderr)
        return 1

if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())
